Echo candidates are real English (Forgot it all, The first day, Bye) except: echo: 'Ashra.' = عشرة (his fix of 13 after her عشاء). Engine wrote هذا الثاني at 43:20; Amal's echo shows حدا التاني. 07:34 engine got على عشرة right (time). 16:54-53:20 is a rule lesson on awal/aa5er/taani/8eir/nafs; slips on it are filed under one PROPOSE rule.
coverage.r2: Opening 00:00-06:40 and 54:16-end are English meta talk. 12:12-15:40 and many drill turns are Latin-transliterated by the engine. Most of 17:00-53:00 is a rule drill on أول/آخر/تاني/غير/نفس, so several rows are rule statements she rejected (medium). No bucket fits the ordinal-position rule, so those rows are PROPOSE. echo: 'Ashra.' (15:44) = عشرة after her عشاء; 'A different person.' / 'The second thing.' are real English translations. 43:20 engine wrote هذا الثاني, her echo shows حدا التاني.

r3_note: D9 (r1) and D15 (r2) are the same plural-agreement slip at 46:02-46:10 (kept once, as D15); D9 is kept as r2's separate الآخر -> الأخير slip at 45:55. D11/D12 filed A7 to match agreed A15 (ordinal with el- before the noun). D1 dropped as engine (he said متأخر right at 07:04). D5 dropped as S4 (dropped final ر in 3ashar).

rows.medi_said: أنا سمعت متأخر اليوم. صحيت. That's right.
rows.why: He said سمعت (I heard) for صحيت (I woke up); her صحيت at 07:06 came before his 'صحيت. That's right.' (GR-24 example).

rows.medi_said: آآآ على عشرة.
rows.why: Clock time takes el-; her whole reply was الـ and he fixed it to على العشرة (GR-25: one A1 el- prompt).

rows.medi_said: Okay أنا شوي-- أنا كان قنيش شوي--
rows.why: kaan must carry the I-ending with أنا (kunt); she said أنا كنت and he repeated أنا كنت شوي.

rows.medi_said: أنا كنت شوي كسول هادي الصباح. هاد الصباح.
rows.amal_said: We never say هذا الصبح just say الصبح or بالصباح.
rows.why: He calqued 'this morning' as هاد الصباح (also هادي الصباح at 08:23); she said we never say that, just الصبح or بالصباح.
rows.english: I was a bit lazy this morning.
rows.proposed_rule: 'This morning' is el-sub7 or bil-saba7, never hada el-saba7 (a calque from English): ana kunet kasool el-sub7

rows.medi_said: أنا لا مش شجاع اليوم. مش شجاع اليوم.
rows.chat: lissa mish mitshajje3 lalshu9ul? / ana la mish mitshajje3
rows.why: She asked لسه مش متشجع and he answered with شجاع (brave), a different word of the same root; she recast متشجع at once. Sheet: motivated | Mitshajje3 | متشجع.
rows.r3_why: Real recast; شجاع (brave) is a different lexical item from متشجع (motivated), so tier 1 not tier 2.

rows.medi_said: أنا لازم آآآ عطلة و
rows.why: laazem went straight onto a noun; she supplied the verb in English ('you should take') and he said أنا لازم أخد عطلة (GR-27).
rows.english: I need to take a vacation.

rows.medi_said: أنا لازم أخد عطلة وسفر، سفر.
rows.why: laazem needs a verb (GR-27): he chained the noun safar after laazem ... u; her English rephrase 'I should travel' (PG-22) made him say ولازم أسافر.
rows.english: I must take a vacation and travel
rows.r3_why: GR-27 / PG-22: after laazem (carried by u) he put the noun سفر where the verb is needed; she gave the verb in English 'I should travel' and he said ولازم أسافر. Grammar B2, not vocab.

rows.medi_said: أنا خططت امم سفر، سفر
rows.why: خطط takes la- (plan for); she said 'You plan for.' and he said لا سفر (la-safar).

rows.medi_said: بس أنا راح آآآ على آآآ عموي.
rows.amal_said: Sorry بس أنا راح what?. ... راح going. What's going؟
rows.why: ra7 needs a verb; she asked 'راح what?' / 'What's going?' and he added أروح (راح أروح).
rows.english: But I'm going to my uncle's for work.

rows.medi_said: آآآ عموي. / and amuwi.
rows.why: He built 'my uncle' as 3ammo + -i; she said عمي twice and he accepted ('That's right'); the fix is the possessive ending on 3am (sheet: uncle (paternal) | 3am | عم).
rows.r3_why: Real recast (عمي twice, he took it 'That's right'); the fix is only the possessive ending on عم, so grammar A4 per the tier-2 note (purely an ending rule = grammar).

rows.medi_said: راح أروح على and عموي.
rows.amal_said: Either على or عند which one؟ Can't put two.
rows.why: He stacked two prepositions على + عند; she said you can't put two, pick one (chat: 3ind).

rows.medi_said: How do I say we will have fun, Rah? Rah bida.
rows.amal_said: No. It's the whole-- It's the reason of our whole one month long lesson.
rows.why: He tried 'Rah bida' for 'we will have fun'; she said No and hinted until he produced ننبسط (sheet: have fun / enjoy | Enbese6). The engine text 'bida' is unclear.

rows.medi_said: Oh my gosh, I forgot the word for, for camping. ... Tesh-teshki?
rows.chat: u ba3dain e7na ra7 nroo7 ta5yeem ba3ed.
rows.why: He forgot camping (sheet: camping | ta5yeem | تخييم), guessed teshki; she hinted خيمة then supplied تخييم.

rows.medi_said: if I say el awal elsaa, that means the f-- the, the... I thought you said this was also the first hour
rows.amal_said: Nothing. ... It would be the first if the أول is after.
rows.why: He put el-awal with el- before the noun; she said it means nothing and the 'the first' form goes after the noun (then الساعة الأولى at 18:31).
rows.r3_why: During the أول recall drill he gave el awal elsaa as a form meaning 'the first hour'; she said 'Nothing' and explained أول must come after. Same pattern as agreed A15 (الأول اليوم -> Nothing), so filed A7 like A15. Medium because it sits inside his English rule recital.

rows.medi_said: So الساعة el awal
rows.amal_said: Yes. بس we learned how to say الأول for a feminine. What is it? Do you remember?
rows.why: ساعة is feminine so the adjective is الأولى; she prompted and he said الساعة الأولى.

rows.medi_said: and التاني الساعة means a different hour.
rows.amal_said: لا. We can't say تاني الساعة. It doesn't mean anything.
rows.chat: taani saa3a = second hour / second hour
rows.why: Ordinal with el- before the noun; she said it doesn't mean anything (ساعة تاني after the noun = a different hour, 22:26).
rows.r3_why: She asked him to apply the أول rule to تاني; he produced التاني الساعة for 'a different hour' and she said 'لا. We can't say تاني الساعة. It doesn't mean anything.' Real explicit-no; filed A7 like D11 / A15.

rows.medi_said: المصاري راح يجي، uh, في... في تاني يوم.
rows.amal_said: No, that's not two days. Second week.
rows.chat: el-masari ra7 yiju fi tani youm / youm tani
rows.why: She had just told him مصاري is plural, so the verb is يجو (her chat yiju); she voiced nothing on the verb.
rows.english: The money will come on the second day.

rows.medi_said: the money will come another day would be المال راح يجي، uh, في يوم تاني.
rows.chat: el masari ra7 yiju el-yom el-tani
rows.why: Spoken word for money is مصاري (sheet: money (plural) | Ma9aari | مصاري), which he used at 23:50; المال is MSA. She did not voice it; her chat writes el masari.
rows.english: the money will come another day
rows.r3_why: He switched to MSA المال a moment after using المصاري; Amal let it pass. Kept as vocab-B (her review), low.

rows.medi_said: هذي اليوم التانية.
rows.amal_said: مم، مم، هذي اليوم. ... مرة، هذي المرة.
rows.chat: hadi el-marra el-tania illi bashufek elyoam
rows.why: He put اليوم (day) where المرة (time) was meant; she echoed هذي اليوم then said مرة، هذي المرة and he redid it.
rows.english: This is the second time (I see you today).

rows.medi_said: So ساعة الأول-- It should be ساعة الأول. ساعة، ساعة أـ...
rows.why: Feminine ساعة needs الأولى and the noun needs el- too; she recast الساعة الأولى.

rows.medi_said: The first day
rows.chat: awal el-sa3a = the beginning of the hour.
rows.why: He misread her أول اليوم as 'the first day'; she repeated it twice until he said 'the beginning of the day' at 30:52.
rows.proposed_rule: أول before a noun with el- means 'the beginning of' (أول اليوم = the beginning of the day); before a bare noun it means 'first' (أول يوم = first day).
rows.r3_why: Real: in the listening drill he read أول اليوم as 'the first day'; she repeated it twice (laughing) until he said 'the beginning of the day'. The point is the أول placement / el- rule, so grammar, listening.

rows.medi_said: الأول اليوم. No, that's the-- Isn't that the first day?
rows.why: Adjective must follow the noun; she said his الأول اليوم means nothing and gave اليوم الأول.
rows.proposed_rule: Tool words awal / aa5er / taani / 8eir go BEFORE a bare noun with no el- (awal saa3a, taani youm, 7ada taani = someone else); AFTER the noun they act as adjectives, take el- with the noun and agree (el-saa3a el-oola); aa5er + el-noun = the end of (aa5er el-ijtimaa3)

rows.medi_said: And then مرة, uh, مرة الأخر.
rows.why: After a noun آخر becomes the adjective أخيرة (taught minutes before); she cued him and he changed to مرة الأخيرة.

rows.medi_said: مرة الأخيرة.
rows.why: Noun + el-adjective needs el- on the noun too; she recast المرة الأخيرة and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: The last person that came.
rows.why: He read her آخر حدا بيجي (present, b-) as past; she stressed 'To come' and he said 'That comes. The last person that comes.'
rows.r3_why: Listening: he read present بيجي as past 'came'; she said 'To come' and he changed to 'That comes'. Tense is a grammar point (b- present), so grammar B1, listening, low.

rows.medi_said: الرحلة أخيرة.
rows.why: Repeating her الرحلة الأخيرة he dropped el- on the adjective (makes a sentence 'the trip is last'); she recast الأخيرة and he repeated it right.
rows.r3_why: Real A7 recast; he was reading back her Arabic in the guess drill (she said الرحلة الأخيرة, he repeated it without el-), so mode listening.

rows.medi_said: غير يوم. غير اليوم. I'll see you another day.
rows.chat: bashufek 8eir yoam = i'll see you another day
rows.why: Right after she said غير takes no el-, reading back her بشوفك غير يوم he said غير اليوم; she repeated غير يوم.
rows.proposed_rule: غير (other / another) never puts el- on the noun after it: بشوفك غير يوم.
rows.r3_why: She said بشوفك غير يوم and asked its meaning; reading it back he said غير يوم then غير اليوم and she re-said غير يوم - a listening read-back slip, kept low because he said it right first.

rows.proposed_rule: Tool words awal / aa5er / taani / 8eir go BEFORE a bare noun with no el- (awal saa3a, taani youm, 7ada taani = someone else); AFTER the noun they act as adjectives, take el- with the noun and agree (el-saa3a el-oola); aa5er + el-noun = the end of (aa5er el-ijtimaa3)

rows.medi_said: Oh, you're right. Uh, هذا الثاني.

rows.proposed_rule: Tool words awal / aa5er / taani / 8eir go BEFORE a bare noun with no el- (awal saa3a, taani youm, 7ada taani = someone else); AFTER the noun they act as adjectives, take el- with the noun and agree (el-saa3a el-oola); aa5er + el-noun = the end of (aa5er el-ijtimaa3)

rows.amal_said: صح. عشر y. ... y عشر not عشرة.

rows.r3_why: Real A8 slip (same slip r1 filed under D9): he gave الأخيرة then masc أخير for plural دقايق; she gave أخيرات and he took it ('Oh, because it's plural').

rows.medi_said: Yeah، آخر الموظفة, right?
